findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the evaluative criterion for `reason_grounded` alongside the sub-answer schema: specify what characteristics of `no_file_impact_reason` make it `yes` (e.g. names each deliverable, provides causal argument why no file edit is needed), `no` (present but unsupported), or `insufficient` (absent or too sparse to evaluate), so the prompt author and the offline oracle both have an unambiguous protocol.
evidence: Plan defines decision rules: 'Set assertion_plausible: yes only when reason_grounded: yes and repo_file_change_named: no' and 'Set assertion_plausible: insufficient when reason_grounded is no or insufficient' — but gives no evaluative definition of what makes a reason 'grounded' vs 'not grounded' vs 'insufficient'.

Existing analogues (necessity.md lines 50-57, asserted_capability.md lines 52-58) each define the evaluation criterion alongside the sub-answer: e.g. 'does the plan REPRODUCE OR CONCRETELY MOTIVATE the current behavior?' and 'does the claim MATCH the code?'. No such definition is given for reason_grounded.

ABSENCE: the plan's 'CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS' contract block names three fields but only one (repo_file_change_named) has a clear enough semantic from its name alone; reason_grounded's meaning is protocol-dependent and left undefined.
findings.finding: The sub-answer `reason_grounded: yes|no|insufficient` drives three distinct outcomes (PASS, advisory contradiction, non-blocking coaching) but the plan never specifies the evaluative criterion — what makes a `no_file_impact_reason` 'grounded' versus 'not grounded' versus 'insufficient' — alongside the decision rules that consume it. A prompt author receives the field name and its downstream role but no definition of the evaluation protocol for assigning it.
findings.location: Plan section 'Criterion judgment and prompt discovery' — `reason_grounded` decision rules
scenarios: A prompt author producing plan_review_no_file_impact.md must independently invent what counts as a 'grounded' reason — e.g. whether naming a specific external system suffices, or whether a causal argument is required — producing inconsistent LLM behavior across prompt revisions.

The offline rubric-behavior test (case 4: 'vague plan with empty or ungrounded reason') requires a definition of 'ungrounded' to write a reliable oracle; without a plan-level definition the test oracle is also underspecified.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'reason_grounded' evaluation clause to the sub-answer contract block: 'reason_grounded: yes when the declared reason names each deliverable and explains why none requires a repo-file edit; no when the reason is present but makes a claim the plan text contradicts or doesn't support; insufficient when reason is empty, one-word, or too sparse to assess.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion verifying that a Pass-1 request for a chunk containing both G5 and `no-file-impact` carries both the `decomp_context` block and the `declared_reason` block, in that stable order.
evidence: Plan body: 'A chunk containing both criteria must receive both blocks in stable order.'
Test Design: 'Also render a chunk containing both G5 and `no-file-impact` and assert both public context blocks reach the LLM request in stable order.'
ABSENCE: No AC reads 'A chunk containing both G5 and no-file-impact criteria receives both context blocks in stable order.'
findings.finding: The plan body explicitly requires that 'A chunk containing both criteria must receive both blocks in stable order' and the Test Design describes asserting this stable-order property, but no acceptance criterion verifies it. This is a described deliverable (the `extra_parts` compositional behavior for mixed G5 + `no-file-impact` chunks) without a covering AC.
findings.location: Approach / 'Declared-reason data flow' subsection; Test Design / 'Prompt-input contract' bullet; Acceptance Criteria (no matching item)
scenarios: An implementer silently drops or reorders the decomp_context block when both criteria are present; no AC fails because AC 9 only checks the reason round-trip for a single-criterion chunk.
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: 'A Pass-1 request for a chunk containing both G5 and `no-file-impact` includes both the decomposition context block and the declared-reason block, in stable order (decomp_context first).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a note in AGENTS.md (or the existing plan-review design doc) describing the `extra_parts` accumulator pattern in `pass1.py` as the canonical extension point for per-criterion prompt context, so future criterion authors know how to follow it.
evidence: 'Replace the single `extra` assignment with compositional `extra_parts`: append `decomp_context` when the chunk contains G5, append the declared-reason block when it contains `no-file-impact`'
No mention of updating AGENTS.md or any design doc with this new dispatch convention
ABSENCE: no ADR/AGENTS.md update is listed in the Scope section
findings.finding: The `extra_parts` compositional dispatch pattern introduced in `pass1.py` (replacing the inline G5-only branch with a generic per-criterion context-block accumulator) is a new architectural pattern that future criterion authors must follow when adding criteria requiring custom prompt context. The plan does not call for capturing this pattern in AGENTS.md, a design doc, or any developer-facing reference.
scenarios: A developer adds a third criterion needing custom prompt context, does not know the `extra_parts` pattern exists, and reverts to an ad-hoc inline branch — fragmenting the architecture silently.
A reviewer inspects `pass1.py` months later with no prior context and cannot determine the intended extension point.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one paragraph to AGENTS.md (or wherever the plan-review architecture is described) explaining: 'To inject per-criterion context into a Pass-1 prompt, append to `extra_parts` inside the chunk loop in `pass1.py`; do not add new inline branches.' Reference the G5 and `no-file-impact` entries as examples.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document `require_file_impact_scope` alongside `require_parent_id` in whatever reference covers valid `applies_at` routing keys (AGENTS.md, the routing-schema README, or a routing-keys guide), so it is discoverable by future criterion authors without reading implementation code.
evidence: 'Extend the shared routing validator in `src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py` to accept a non-empty list of non-empty strings for the new key'
'Add `applies_at.require_file_impact_scope: ["none"]` to the packaged routing entry'
ABSENCE: no AGENTS.md or routing-schema doc update appears in the Scope section
findings.finding: The new `require_file_impact_scope` routing key is a new extension point in the shared routing schema, validated in `overlay.py` and used in `registry.applies(...)`. The plan lists it in the Scope but does not call for updating any developer-facing routing-schema reference (AGENTS.md, a routing-keys guide, or the existing routing documentation) so that future criterion authors know this axis exists.
scenarios: A future criterion author wants to filter by file_impact_scope but cannot discover `require_file_impact_scope` without reading `overlay.py` source code.
The routing schema grows routing axes that are undocumented, making the overlay validator the de-facto (and fragile) source of truth.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add at least one observable signal (debug log line or counter) for (a) when the `file_impact_scope` routing predicate selects or skips `no-file-impact` and (b) when the LLM call for this criterion fails or is skipped via fail-open.
evidence: 'the existing advisory Pass-1 framework already owns LLM execution and fail-open behavior' — the plan delegates error handling but does not add any logging/metric/trace for the new criterion's call or routing decision
ABSENCE: no mention of log lines, counters, or traces for the new `no-file-impact` LLM invocation or the `file_impact_scope`-based routing branch
findings.finding: The plan adds a new LLM call path (routing `no-file-impact` to the LLM via Pass 1) and new routing logic, but specifies no observability instrumentation — no log entry, metric, or trace — for the new failure point, making it impossible for operators to distinguish a routing miss, an LLM timeout, or a silent fail-open from a correct PASS.
findings.location: Approach / Criterion judgment and prompt discovery; Approach / Deterministic applicability
scenarios: LLM provider times out for `no-file-impact` specifically — operator cannot tell whether the criterion was skipped, failed, or passed
Routing predicate silently excludes the criterion due to a future state-key rename — no observable signal that the criterion never ran
findings.suggested_fix: In `registry.py`, log at DEBUG level when `no-file-impact` is selected or excluded by the `file_impact_scope` check. In `pass1.py` (or the existing fail-open handler), log at WARNING when the `no-file-impact` LLM call is dropped due to an error, including the criterion name and scope value.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (or plan note) specifying the `rebar explain no-file-impact` exit code and message when the criterion exists in the registry but the generated guide entry is absent.
evidence: AC text: 'rebar explain no-file-impact succeeds with the generated criterion documentation' — only a success assertion
ABSENCE: no AC or plan text addresses what `rebar explain` outputs or exits with if `no-file-impact` is missing from the generated guide or the registry
findings.finding: The `rebar explain no-file-impact` AC covers only the success path; the plan does not specify behavior when the criterion ID is unrecognized or when the generated documentation is absent (e.g., before the first guide regeneration).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — '`rebar explain no-file-impact` succeeds with the generated criterion documentation.'
scenarios: Developer runs `rebar explain no-file-impact` on a branch where the guide has not yet been regenerated — unclear whether the command errors cleanly or produces a confusing empty/partial output

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify whether file_impact_scope is read from ctx.state inside route_criteria (no signature change, no caller updates needed) or threaded as a new route_criteria parameter (requiring workflow_ops.py and production_batch_runner.py to be added to Scope).
evidence: workflow_ops.py:256: single, agent = orchestrator.route_criteria(pctx)
production_batch_runner.py:245: single, agent = route_criteria(ctx)

orchestrator.py:374-380: the only call to registry.applies(), inside route_criteria which already reads ctx.state.get('parent_id') internally — establishing the pattern for reading state inside route_criteria rather than threading through the signature
Scope section lists only: reviewers/plan_review_no_file_impact.md, criteria_routing.json, overlay.py, registry.py, orchestrator.py, pass1.py, docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md
findings.finding: The plan's 'single orchestrator call site' phrasing is ambiguous about whether file_impact_scope becomes a new parameter on route_criteria's signature or is read from ctx.state inside route_criteria. If route_criteria's signature grows a file_impact_scope parameter, two callers outside the Scope list become unenumerated consumers: workflow_ops.plan_review_assemble_criteria (workflow_ops.py:256) and production_batch_runner._project_criteria (production_batch_runner.py:245), neither of which is listed in the plan's Scope section.
findings.location: Approach / Deterministic applicability — 'Pass ctx.state.get("file_impact_scope") at the single orchestrator call site'; Scope section omits workflow_ops.py and production_batch_runner.py
scenarios: If the implementer adds file_impact_scope as a parameter to route_criteria's signature (matching the has_parent pattern at the applies() call), both workflow_ops.py and production_batch_runner.py fail to compile / produce wrong routing behavior until updated.

If the implementer reads ctx.state.get('file_impact_scope') inside route_criteria (directly, without adding it to route_criteria's signature), no caller update is needed and the Scope list is complete — but the plan doesn't make this choice explicit.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Deterministic applicability section: 'Read ctx.state.get("file_impact_scope") inside route_criteria and forward it to registry.applies() — do not add file_impact_scope to route_criteria's public signature, so workflow_ops.py and production_batch_runner.py require no changes.' This matches the existing pattern where route_criteria reads ctx.state.get('parent_id') to compute has_parent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the `applies_at.require_file_impact_scope` validator extension, explicitly specify: (1) the list must be non-empty, (2) every member must be a non-empty string, and (3) document what `applies()` returns when the list is present but empty (should be treated as a misconfiguration error, not silently fail-closed).
evidence: Plan states: 'Extend the shared routing validator in src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py to accept a non-empty list of non-empty strings for the new key.'
Existing validator validates `require_parent_id` as a boolean (overlay.py lines 218-222) with an explicit type check and a located CriteriaError.

The plan states the validation rule in one phrase but does not specify that `applies()` must short-circuit cleanly on `[]` (empty list passes the non-empty check but the member-of test always returns False) vs. raising vs. treating as absent.
AC 'The packaged routing entry passes shared validation' implies the validator runs but doesn't specify what constitutes a passing vs. failing entry for the new key.
findings.finding: The plan specifies extending `_validate_routing_entry` in `overlay.py` to accept `require_file_impact_scope` but does not specify what validation rules apply to malformed values (e.g. an empty list `[]`, a list containing integers, or a list containing empty strings). Without precise validation rules, a malformed packaged entry could pass the CI parity gate (`validate_packaged_routing`) and silently misconfigure the criterion — causing `no-file-impact` to never select (empty list) or to select on garbage values, depending on how the `applies()` predicate handles unexpected input.
scenarios: A future overlay author writes `require_file_impact_scope: []` — with a lenient validator this passes CI but `no-file-impact` is never selected for any ticket (the member-of test on an empty list is always False).

A future overlay author writes `require_file_impact_scope: ["none", ""]` — an empty-string member could match a ticket whose `file_impact_scope` is an empty string rather than missing, producing a spurious selection.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_validate_routing_entry`, after confirming `require_file_impact_scope` is a list, add: `if not rfs or any(not isinstance(s, str) or not s for s in rfs): raise CriteriaError(...)` — mirroring the `scope` validator's non-empty + member-validity check at lines 205-213.

findings.finding: The AC 'Review of every new test confirms it asserts observable behavior, serialized/public contracts, or persisted state; none greps source text or asserts private implementation shape' is effort/process-framed ('review of every new test') and has no concrete proving command — it describes a human review action rather than a specific observable, deterministic outcome.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Review of every new test confirms it asserts observable behavior...'
findings.suggested_fix: Remove this item from the formal AC list (it is already covered by the Test Design prose 'Tests assert observable behavior and public contracts, never grep source text or depend on private implementation shape') and instead add a short CI-checkable rule — e.g., a custom pylint/flake8 plugin or an agreed naming convention — that makes the constraint mechanical. If no automation is feasible, state the reviewing convention explicitly and mark the criterion [operator-attested].

findings.finding: The `_chunk` closure in `pass1.py` passes a single `extra` string to `_pass1_with_ladder`. The plan extends the G5-only branch to also handle `no-file-impact`, but does not specify that the two extra-context strings must be concatenated when both G5 and `no-file-impact` land in the same facet chunk. Both criteria share `facet: scope-intent` (confirmed from existing prompt files), so on a `file_impact_scope == 'none'` ticket they will co-chunk. The plan's proposed branch — `extra = decomp_context if any(G5) else ''` extended with `any(no-file-impact)` — results in a mutual-exclusion pattern that loses one context block when both criteria are co-chunked.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single-winner pattern with: `extras = [decomp_context] if any(c.get('id') == 'G5' for c in chunk) else []; if any(c.get('id') == 'no-file-impact' for c in chunk): extras.append(<declared_reason_block>); extra = '\n\n'.join(e for e in extras if e)`

findings.finding: The plan assigns `no-file-impact` to `facet: scope-intent`, the same facet as G5. `chunk_by_facet()` packs same-facet 1-TURN criteria together, so when a ticket has `file_impact_scope: none` AND children, both G5 and `no-file-impact` land in the same chunk. `pass1.py`'s `_chunk()` uses a single `extra_context: str` parameter. The plan extends the branch with `any(c.get('id') == 'no-file-impact' for c in chunk)` but does not specify how `decomp_context` (the G5 injection) and the `declared_reason` block (the `no-file-impact` injection) are combined when both criteria co-reside in a chunk. The naive if/elif extension supplies only one context string, silently dropping the other.
findings.location: Declared-reason data flow section; `pass1.py` `_chunk()` function (line 418 in current codebase)
findings.suggested_fix: Change the `_chunk` extra-context logic to build `extra` by concatenating all applicable context blocks: `extra = '\n\n'.join(filter(None, [decomp_context if any G5 else '', declared_reason_block if any no-file-impact else '']))`. This is order-stable and additive, so the G5 and no-file-impact paths both get their required context. Document the concatenation order (decomp first, declared-reason second) so the prompt structure is reproducible.

findings.finding: AC 17 mixes an in-session-verifiable constraint ('no source-grep/change-detector tests are added') with a forward-looking design principle ('remain green under behavior-preserving refactors') that cannot be verified within the session. An agent completing this work has no deterministic in-session command that proves the forward-looking part; it is guidance, not a measurable criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'New tests are behavior/contract-focused and remain green under behavior-preserving refactors; no source-grep/change-detector tests are added.'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single AC with: (a) '[ ] No new test uses source-file grep, internal symbol name matching, or change-detector assertions — confirmed by code review of added test files.' and move 'remain green under behavior-preserving refactors' to the Test Design section as an authoring guideline rather than an acceptance criterion.
